chunks: Sahl ibn Ziyād narrated from ʿAlī ibn Asbāṭ, from ʿAlī ibn Jaʿfar, who said:

My brother Mūsā عليه السلام informed me, saying: “I was standing by my father’s head when the messenger of Ziyād ibn ʿUbayd Allāh al-Ḥārithī, the governor of al-Madīnah, came to him and said: ‘The amīr says to you: come to me.’ He excused himself on account of an illness. Then the messenger returned to him and said to him: ‘I have ordered that the gate of the enclosed area be opened for you, for it is nearer for your steps.’ He said: Then my father rose and leaned on me, and entered upon the governor, who had gathered all the jurists of the people of al-Madīnah. Before him was a document containing testimony against a man from the people of Wādī al-Qurā, who had mentioned the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم and spoken against him.”

The governor said to him: ‘O Abā ʿAbd Allāh, examine this document.’ He said: ‘Not until I see what they have said.’ He said: Then he turned to them and said: ‘What did you say?’ They said: ‘We said he should be disciplined, beaten, punished, and imprisoned.’ He said: Then he said to them: ‘Tell me, if he had mentioned a man from among the companions of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, what would the ruling concerning him have been?’ They said: ‘The same as this.’ He said: ‘So there is no difference between the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم and a man from among his companions?’ He said: Then the governor said: ‘Leave these people aside, O Abā ʿAbd Allāh. If we had wanted these people, we would not have sent for you.’

He said: Then Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام said: ‘My father informed me that the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم said: “The people are alike and equal regarding me. Whoever hears someone mentioning me, then it is obligatory upon him to kill whoever insults me, and he is not to be referred to the authority. And it is obligatory upon the authority, if he is referred to it, to kill whoever speaks against me.”’
He said: ‘Then Ziyād ibn ʿUbayd Allāh said: “Take this man out and kill him according to the judgment of Abū ʿAbd Allāh.”’

key_terms.أُسْوَةٌ: equal standing, meaning people are alike with respect to the Prophet’s inviolability
key_terms.السُّلْطَانِ: the ruling authority or state power
key_terms.الْوَالِي: the governor or political authority presiding over the case
key_terms.شَتَمَنِي: insulted me; used here for reviling the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
key_terms.شَهَادَةٌ: formal testimony recorded against the accused man
key_terms.فُقَهَاءَ: jurists consulted regarding the legal ruling
key_terms.نَالَ مِنِّي: spoke against me or dishonored me

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling in Shia hadith on a person who insults the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم?
ai.summary: This hadith narrates an incident in which Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام was consulted by the governor of al-Madīnah regarding a man accused of reviling the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم. The Imam عليه السلام reports a statement from the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم establishing the ruling in such a case, after dismissing the lesser opinions of the gathered jurists. The report is significant for its legal content and for showing the Imam’s religious authority in a judicial matter.
